messages.subject: International mobility of researchers
messages.body_plain:
Dear Sir/Madam,

Stimulating knowledge exchange through mobility of researchers has become a key priority to national and European policy makers. However, a lot is still not fully understood and more evidence is needed to develop effective policies on this topic. To this end, the European Commission has launched a large scale study (known as the MORE-study - www.researchersmobility.eu) focusing on mobility patterns and career paths of researchers.

We would like to invite you to participate to our survey (about 10-15 minutes of your time) in order to collect your experiences with respect to mobility. Your opinion on the problems, needs and attitudes will help the European Commission (and other Governments) to develop better targeted policies on this subject.

All completed surveys shall remain strictly private and confidential and shall only be used for the purposes of this study.

Please click here to start the survey:
http://s.checkmarket.com/?e=13049&c=4540162&l=en&h=AB2064CABD4A9422DB75


Thank you in advance for your survey participation and feedback.

If you encounter any technical difficulties taking the survey, please contact us at EC-study at researchersmobility.eu

Sincerely yours,

Arnold Verbeek
(project director)

Recently, we invited you to participate in our survey. Until now, you have not yet responded. We kindly ask you to take about 15 minutes to complete the survey.

This project is funded by the European Commission, Directorate General for Research

Please click here to start the survey:
http://s.checkmarket.com/?e=13049&c=4540162&l=en&h=AB2064CABD4A9422DB75

Stimulating knowledge exchange through mobility of researchers has become a key priority to national and European policy makers. However, a lot is still not fully understood and more evidence is needed to develop effective policies on this topic. To this end, the European Commission has launched a large scale study (known as the MORE-study - www.researchersmobility.eu) focusing on mobility patterns and career paths of researchers.

We would like to invite you to participate to our survey (about 10-15 minutes of your time) in order to collect your experiences with respect to mobility. Your opinion on the problems, needs and attitudes will help the European Commission (and other Governments) to develop better targeted policies on this subject.

messages.subject: CRAN packages maintained by you
messages.body_plain:
Dear maintainers,

This concerns the packages

  BioStatR BiplotGUI GAMens MChtest NestedCohort REEMtree ROCR RQDA SGP
  ca choplump dirmult dlm emdbook extremevalues fPortfolio gene2pathway
  lemma mclust mixlow plotrix primer randomSurvivalForest rattle
  rconifers season ssanv tweedie

maintained by one of you.

These packages have a file CITATION (in the top-level package source
directory), where R really uses inst/CITATION.

Can we pls have updates with the citation file in the right place?

Please also ensure that your citation file does not make calls to
packageDescription() or alike to access the package metadata.  Instead,
please require at least R >= 2.8.0, and use a variable called 'meta' in
your code which will be passed on automagically to citation().  I.e.,
instead of e.g.

  desc <- packageDescription("mixlow")
  year <- sub(".*(2[[:digit:]]{3})-.*", "\\1", desc$Date)
  vers <- paste("R package version", desc$Version)

use

  year <- sub(".*(2[[:digit:]]{3})-.*", "\\1", meta$Date)
  vers <- paste("R package version", meta$Version)

If requiring R >= 2.8.0 is a problem, use e.g.

  if(!exists("meta") || is.null(meta)) meta <- packageDescription("mixlow")
  year <- sub(".*(2[[:digit:]]{3})-.*", "\\1", meta$Date)
  vers <- paste("R package version", meta$Version)

I find such (and other) problems in the CITATION files for

  BioStatR REEMtree ROCR RQDA dirmult dlm emdbook extremevalues
  fPortfolio gene2pathway lemma mclust mixlow plotrix primer
  randomSurvivalForest rattle rconifers season

Best
-k

messages.subject_clean: ARCH and GARCH implementations in CRAN
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I have been playing around with R as applied to Jim Hamilton's 1994 "Time Series Analysis" text.  I found at least two seemingly applicable implementations in CRAN, garch in package "tseries", and garchFit in package "fGarch".  What is a little strange, however, is that it doesn't seem to be possible to fit a simple ARCH specification (i.e. a GARCH(0,q)) that also simultaneously estimates regression coefficients as described on page 660 of Hamilton's book.  As near as I can tell "garch" has no place to specify such a regression, whereas garchFit does, but garch assumes the "p" of a GARCH(p,q) is greater than zero.

Is this a correct assessment of the capabilities of these two packages?

Thanks,
Robert Bell CFA,
Wilmington, DE
